\mxunit{enrichment-inequalities-solutions}{Inequalities and equality cases}
\mxsubtitle{High school · optimisation and olympiads \textperiodcentered{} Worked solutions \textperiodcentered{} 11}

\begin{exercise}
For $x>0$, prove $x+\frac{1}{x}\geq 2$ and determine equality.
\end{exercise}
\begin{solution}
$x+\frac{1}{x}-2=\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{x}\geq 0$. Equality holds exactly at $x=1$.
\end{solution}

\begin{exercise}
Find the minimum of $x^{2}-6x+13$ on $\R $.
\end{exercise}
\begin{solution}
$x^{2}-6x+13=(x-3)^{2}+4\geq 4$. The minimum 4 is attained at $x=3$.
\end{solution}

\begin{exercise}
A rectangle has perimeter 24 m. What is its greatest area?
\end{exercise}
\begin{solution}
Its sides $a,b>0$ satisfy $a+b=12$. Thus $ab\leq 36$, with equality at $a=b=6\,\mathrm{m}$. The maximum area is $36\,\mathrm{m}^{2}$.
\end{solution}

\begin{exercise}
For real a,b, prove $a^{2}+b^{2}\geq 2ab$. Must a and b be positive?
\end{exercise}
\begin{solution}
$a^{2}+b^{2}-2ab=(a-b)^{2}\geq 0$ for all real a,b. No positivity is needed; equality means $a=b$.
\end{solution}

\begin{problem}[Investigate, justify, conclude]
There are 40 m of fencing for three sides of a rectangular enclosure against a wall. Its width x, perpendicular to the wall, is positive. Express its length and area in terms of x, determine the domain, then prove the maximum area without derivatives. Compare with a fully fenced rectangle of perimeter 40 m.
\end{problem}
\begin{solution}
Length is $40-2x$ and $0<x<20$. Area is $A(x)=x(40-2x)=200-2(x-10)^{2}\leq 200$. Equality occurs at width 10 m and length 20 m: $200\,\mathrm{m}^{2}$. With all four sides fenced, $a+b=20$ and the maximum area is $100\,\mathrm{m}^{2}$, attained by a square of side 10 m.
\end{solution}
